# `m.indices.values`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Index levels, tick by tick, as computed by the index providers.

```python
m.indices.values(symbols)
```

| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `blink()`, `append_only()`, `ring()`, `last_by()`, `history()` |
| Served by | flat files, WebSocket |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Indices with the `I:` prefix, such as `"I:SPX"` (`"SPX"` is refused), or `dm.ALL`. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and the rows of each one you delete leave the table. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Values (flat files) | Value (WebSocket) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Indices Basic | Not included | Not included |
| Indices Starter | End-of-day, All history | 15-minute delayed |
| Indices Advanced | End-of-day, All history | Real-time |
| Indices Business | End-of-day, All history | Real-time |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From flat files `ticker`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under."; WebSocket `T`: "The assigned ticker of the index." | flat files, WebSocket |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the row, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the New York date of `Timestamp`. | flat files, WebSocket |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's primary time, as an Instant. From flat files `timestamp`: "The timestamp in Unix MS."; WebSocket `t`: "The Timestamp in Unix MS." | flat files, WebSocket |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | flat files, WebSocket |
| `Value` | double | The value of the index. | flat files, WebSocket |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | flat files, WebSocket |
